newsitem.title: CANADA: Hudson's Bay optimistic about Q4.
newsitem.headline: Hudson's Bay optimistic about Q4.

text.p: Hudson's Bay Co, Canada's largest department store chain, said on Thursday that it saw an improved fourth quarter once consumers took advantage of lower interest rates.

"We are optimistic about continued improvement in the crucial fourth quarter," Hudson's Bay said in reporting higher third-quarter earnings. "The retail climate should benefit from the combination of low rates of interest and inflation and from tax reductions for many consumers."
Canada's central bank has cut interest rates by five percentage points since May 1995.
Canadian inflation is near 1.2 percent and the Ontario government has implemented the first part of its planned 30 percent provincial tax cut for residents.
Hudson's Bay, which owns The Bay department stores and Zellers discount department chain, also reported third quarter earnings of C$0.14 for the period ended Oct. 31 compared to year earlier C$0.04.

During the third quarter, the 101-store Bay chain opened one store and expanded another. Zellers, which has about 300 outlets, unveiled three new ones, enlarged five and closed one. During the rest of the fiscal year Zellers will open two more stores, expand another five and close two.
